name: Speedy
tagline: Tiny main-memory SQL database for Windows and Linux built to make unit testing easy; last updated 2003.
description: Speedy was a one-person project by Harald Wabnig: a small client/server main-memory SQL database, plus Speedy1, a variant linked straight into the application so end users never install a database. It was built to support unit-test environments, with sub-selects, joins, DISTINCT, cursors, transactions and unique indexes through a C API, and came with a viewer, a designer and code generators. The author listed its limits plainly: data must fit in virtual memory, no network access, transactions lock the whole database and query optimisation is manual. The last version, 2.0.1, came out in July 2003; the site still hosts the downloads.
statusNote: Downloads remain online, but the last release was 2.0.1 (July 2003) and development stopped. Use SQLite or DuckDB for embedded SQL in tests.

scale.notes: Whole database must fit in virtual memory on one machine.

strengths: Very small footprint with both client/server and linked-in variants
Supports sub-selects, joins, cursors and transactions despite its size
weaknesses: No network access and whole-database locking during transactions
Incomplete SQL (no views, privileges or ALTER TABLE)
useCases: Historical reference for small embedded SQL engines
Legacy C test harnesses that already use it
